setupText: Mina has a new job at a hotel. She starts on Monday.
text: Mina has a new job at a hotel. She starts on Monday. What does Mina have?
options: a room she has booked
a holiday she has planned
a visit to meet a friend
work she will be paid to do
answer: work she will be paid to do
explanation: A job here is paid work at the hotel.

rationales.a room she has booked: A guest books a room; a job is work, not accommodation.
rationales.work she will be paid to do: A job here is paid work at the hotel.
rationales.a holiday she has planned: Starting a job means starting work, not taking a holiday.
rationales.a visit to meet a friend: A social visit is not a job.

sentence: Who is Ana in relation to the cook?
setupText: 'My boss is Ana,' says a cook at the restaurant.
taskText: Who is Ana in relation to the cook?
text: 'My boss is Ana,' says a cook at the restaurant. Who is Ana in relation to the cook?
options: a person who eats there
a person who delivers food
a person in charge of the cook's work
a person who works under the cook
answer: a person in charge of the cook's work
explanation: Your boss is the person you work under.

rationales.a person who eats there: A person eating there is a customer, not necessarily the cook's boss.
rationales.a person who delivers food: Delivery work does not make someone the cook's boss.
rationales.a person who works under the cook: That reverses the relationship: the boss directs the cook's work.
rationales.a person in charge of the cook's work: Your boss is the person you work under.

setupText: The garage will pay Luis for his work on Friday.
text: The garage will pay Luis for his work on Friday. What will the garage do?
options: give Luis money
ask Luis for money
give Luis another job
ask Luis to take a rest
answer: give Luis money
explanation: 'Pay someone for work' means give that person money for doing it.

rationales.give Luis money: 'Pay someone for work' means give that person money for doing it.
rationales.ask Luis for money: That reverses the payment: the garage is paying Luis.
rationales.give Luis another job: Payment rewards work; it does not mean assigning more work.
rationales.ask Luis to take a rest: A rest is a break, not payment.

setupText: A museum door says 'Staff only.'
text: A museum door says 'Staff only.' Who is this entrance for?
options: people visiting the museum
people buying tickets
people waiting for a tour
people who work at the museum
answer: people who work at the museum
explanation: Staff are the people employed to work in an organization.

rationales.people visiting the museum: Visitors are not staff simply because they enter the museum.
rationales.people buying tickets: Buying admission makes someone a visitor, not a staff member.
rationales.people who work at the museum: Staff are the people employed to work in an organization.
rationales.people waiting for a tour: Tour groups are visitors; this entrance is for workers.

setupText: Omar's shift at the bakery is from six until two.
text: Omar's shift at the bakery is from six until two. What do these times describe?
options: when Omar travels to work
when Omar is scheduled to work
when Omar takes his lunch break
when Omar buys his groceries
answer: when Omar is scheduled to work
explanation: A shift is a set period during which someone works.

rationales.when Omar travels to work: The journey is separate from his scheduled work period.
rationales.when Omar is scheduled to work: A shift is a set period during which someone works.
rationales.when Omar takes his lunch break: A break is a pause within work, not the whole shift.
rationales.when Omar buys his groceries: A work shift does not describe personal shopping.

setupText: 'The keys are in my office, beside my computer,' says the school manager.
text: 'The keys are in my office, beside my computer,' says the school manager. Where should you look?
options: in the room where meals are cooked
in the room where visitors sleep
in the room where the manager works
in the room where cars are kept
answer: in the room where the manager works
explanation: An office is a room or place used for work such as administration.

rationales.in the room where the manager works: An office is a room or place used for work such as administration.
rationales.in the room where meals are cooked: That is a kitchen; office does not name a cooking room.
rationales.in the room where visitors sleep: That is a guest room, not the manager's office.
rationales.in the room where cars are kept: A garage holds cars; an office is used for other work.

setupText: A factory needs three more workers to pack boxes.
text: A factory needs three more workers to pack boxes. What does it need?
options: three more people to do the packing
three more people to buy the boxes
three more people to visit the factory
three more people to inspect a purchase
answer: three more people to do the packing
explanation: A worker is a person doing work; the sentence specifies packing.

rationales.three more people to buy the boxes: Buyers are customers; workers do the packing.
rationales.three more people to visit the factory: Visitors need not do the factory's work.
rationales.three more people to inspect a purchase: Inspecting a purchase is not the packing role described.
rationales.three more people to do the packing: A worker is a person doing work; the sentence specifies packing.

sentence: What will the team do at ten?
setupText: Our team has a meeting about the new menu at ten.
taskText: What will the team do at ten?
text: Our team has a meeting about the new menu at ten. What will the team do at ten?
options: stop work to eat their own meals
serve the first customers
come together to discuss the menu
leave the restaurant for the day
answer: come together to discuss the menu
explanation: A meeting brings people together for discussion or shared business.

rationales.stop work to eat their own meals: A meeting about a menu is a discussion, not necessarily a meal.
rationales.serve the first customers: Serving customers is different from meeting to discuss work.
rationales.come together to discuss the menu: A meeting brings people together for discussion or shared business.
rationales.leave the restaurant for the day: A meeting is an activity at work, not the end of the working day.

setupText: We take a ten-minute break at eleven, then return to work.
text: We take a ten-minute break at eleven, then return to work. What happens during the break?
options: We finish our jobs for the day.
We stop working for a short time.
We begin a different job.
We work faster than before.
answer: We stop working for a short time.
explanation: A break is a temporary pause, followed here by returning to work.

A break is a temporary pause, followed here by returning to work.
They return after ten minutes; the working day is not over.
A break pauses work rather than changing the task.
Working faster is still working, not taking a break.

setupText: 'Your first task is to put labels on these jars.'
text: 'Your first task is to put labels on these jars.' What does 'task' mean here?
options: the piece of work you must do
the person you work for
the place where you work
the time you can go home
answer: the piece of work you must do
explanation: Putting labels on jars is a particular task within the job.

rationales.the person you work for: A task is work to do, not the person assigning it.
rationales.the place where you work: The jars may be at a workstation, but task names the activity.
rationales.the time you can go home: A finishing time is not a task.
rationales.the piece of work you must do: Putting labels on jars is a particular task within the job.

sentence: Eva is going for a job ___.
setupText: The hotel wants to meet Eva and ask her about her work before giving her a job.
taskText: Eva is going for a job ___.
text: The hotel wants to meet Eva and ask her about her work before giving her a job. Eva is going for a job ___.
options: break
interview
shift
holiday
answer: interview
focusKey: coverage-workplace-vocabulary-a1-4091:Job interview as an employment meeting
explanation: A job interview is a meeting where an employer asks an applicant questions.

rationales.break: A break pauses work; this meeting is part of applying for work.
rationales.interview: A job interview is a meeting where an employer asks an applicant questions.
rationales.shift: A shift is scheduled work after someone has the job.
rationales.holiday: A holiday is time off, not a meeting to discuss getting a job.

setupText: Ben repairs shoes. A customer brings him a broken boot.
text: Ben repairs shoes. A customer brings him a broken boot. Who is the customer?
options: the person who teaches Ben repairs
the person who works for Ben
the person who sells tools to Ben
the person using Ben's repair service
answer: the person using Ben's repair service
explanation: A customer buys goods or uses a business's services, such as shoe repair.

rationales.the person who teaches Ben repairs: A teacher may train Ben, but customer names the person using his service.
rationales.the person who works for Ben: An employee works for him; a customer brings work to his business.
rationales.the person using Ben's repair service: A customer buys goods or uses a business's services, such as shoe repair.
rationales.the person who sells tools to Ben: That person supplies Ben; the customer here brings a boot for repair.

setupText: I work in the cleaning team at the airport.
text: I work in the cleaning team at the airport. What does 'team' name?
options: the list of things I need to clean
the building where I keep my tools
the group I work with
the hours when I do the cleaning
answer: the group I work with
explanation: A team is a group working together toward a shared purpose.

rationales.the list of things I need to clean: A list of tasks is not the people doing them.
rationales.the building where I keep my tools: A team is people, not their storage place.
rationales.the hours when I do the cleaning: Work hours describe a shift, not a team.
rationales.the group I work with: A team is a group working together toward a shared purpose.

setupText: Please put the papers on my desk, beside the keyboard.
text: Please put the papers on my desk, beside the keyboard. Which object is the desk?
options: the chair I sit on
the cupboard I hang clothes in
the bag I carry to work
the table I use for work
answer: the table I use for work
explanation: A desk is a worktable, often holding papers or a computer.

rationales.the table I use for work: A desk is a worktable, often holding papers or a computer.
rationales.the chair I sit on: The chair is a seat; the desk is the work surface.
rationales.the cupboard I hang clothes in: A cupboard stores things; desk names the table here.
rationales.the bag I carry to work: A bag may carry papers, but it is not a desk.

setupText: 'Please phone the driver. Do not send a text.'
text: 'Please phone the driver. Do not send a text.' What should you do?
options: speak to the driver in a call
write the driver a short message
write down the driver's number
wait for the driver to call you
answer: speak to the driver in a call
explanation: 'Phone' is a verb here: make a telephone call to someone.

rationales.write the driver a short message: The instruction explicitly asks for a call instead of a text.
rationales.speak to the driver in a call: 'Phone' is a verb here: make a telephone call to someone.
rationales.write down the driver's number: Recording a number does not contact the driver.
rationales.wait for the driver to call you: The instruction asks you to make the call.

sentence: What is kept in this file?
setupText: The blue file contains all the papers about the kitchen repairs.
taskText: What is kept in this file?
text: The blue file contains all the papers about the kitchen repairs. What is kept in this file?
options: documents about the repair work
tools for repairing the kitchen
food for the kitchen staff
money to pay the repair workers
answer: documents about the repair work
explanation: A paper file keeps related documents together.

rationales.tools for repairing the kitchen: Tools do the repairs; this file holds information about them.
rationales.food for the kitchen staff: The file is for papers, not food storage.
rationales.documents about the repair work: A paper file keeps related documents together.
rationales.money to pay the repair workers: Bills may be filed, but a file is not the payment itself.

sentence: What should you do to complete the form?
setupText: On your first day, you receive a form with spaces for your name and address.
taskText: What should you do to complete the form?
text: On your first day, you receive a form with spaces for your name and address. What should you do to complete the form?
options: write a story about your first day
draw a map of the building
give the requested information
make a list of questions for your boss
answer: give the requested information
explanation: To complete this form, fill its spaces with the information requested.

rationales.give the requested information: To complete this form, fill its spaces with the information requested.
rationales.write a story about your first day: A form asks for particular details, not a free-form story.
rationales.draw a map of the building: The spaces request a name and address, not a building map.
rationales.make a list of questions for your boss: Your questions do not complete the requested personal details.

sentence: What does 'sale' mean in this notice?
setupText: 'Our summer sale ends today. Tomorrow these shirts go back to their usual prices.'
taskText: What does 'sale' mean in this notice?
text: 'Our summer sale ends today. Tomorrow these shirts go back to their usual prices.' What does 'sale' mean in this notice?
options: a day when the shop is closed
a time when goods cost less than usual
a delivery of new shirts
a change in the shop's owner
answer: a time when goods cost less than usual
explanation: A sale can mean a period of reduced prices, as the return to usual prices shows.

rationales.a day when the shop is closed: The shop is selling shirts; sale does not mean closure.
rationales.a delivery of new shirts: A delivery brings stock; the notice concerns prices.
rationales.a change in the shop's owner: Nothing here concerns ownership of the business.
rationales.a time when goods cost less than usual: A sale can mean a period of reduced prices, as the return to usual prices shows.

setupText: I work part-time at a bookshop: just two afternoons a week.
text: I work part-time at a bookshop: just two afternoons a week. What does 'part-time' tell you?
options: I work there for no money.
I work fewer hours than a full-time worker.
I work in two different shops.
I work there only while travelling.
answer: I work fewer hours than a full-time worker.
explanation: Part-time work uses only part of the usual full working week.

'Part-time' describes working hours, not whether the work is paid.
rationales.I work fewer hours than a full-time work: Part-time work uses only part of the usual full working week.
Two afternoons do not mean two employers; 'part-time' concerns hours.
'Part-time' does not describe a travel arrangement.

sentence: Where should you look for the room number?
setupText: 'I sent you an email with tomorrow's room number.'
taskText: Where should you look for the room number?
text: 'I sent you an email with tomorrow's room number.' Where should you look for the room number?
options: on a paper notice by the door
in a recorded phone message
on a printed envelope in the post
in your email messages
answer: in your email messages
explanation: An email is an electronic message sent to an email address.

rationales.on a paper notice by the door: A notice is not the email the speaker sent.
rationales.in a recorded phone message: An email is written electronic communication, not a voice recording.
rationales.in your email messages: An email is an electronic message sent to an email address.
rationales.on a printed envelope in the post: Postal mail is different from an email message.
